notes:
Summary: DevFlow is a YC-ish startup building a VS Code extension copilot (marketplace listed). Primary ask = low-latency streaming inline suggestions + robust model/version pinning per-customer.

POC scope: 1) Measure median token latency under real extension traffic (local dev machines, ~350 active users internal), 2) Verify model pinning & fallback to cheaper quantized variant for low-priority completions, 3) Validate auth flow (SSO/OAuth) + per-org and per-user rate limits.

Quotes / highlights:
- CTO (R. Patel): "We need inline suggestions to feel instant — target <50ms median token latency from our extension client to completion token delivery."
- Engineering lead: "Version pinning is critical. We must be able to pin customers to a vetted 7B quantized model and rollback quickly if a quality regression shows up."

Technical constraints / requirements (from call):
- Extension uses a thin websocket for streaming; expects chunked token streams and reconnect + resume semantics.
- Must support per-user rate limits (burst and sustained) and org-level quotas for marketplace tiering.
- Need token-level cost visibility for our billing pipeline and token-usage webhooks.
- Data residency: primary engineering data in NA, but support EU for some customers (want routing/by-region).

Security & procurement notes:
- Security questionnaire (sent 2025-12-01) — awaiting SOC2 report and KMS integration docs.
- Legal flagged vendor lock-in concerns; asked for exportability of pinned model configs and audit logs.

POC results so far (short):
- Hosted API (us-west) with streaming: median token latency ~65ms — borderline vs their target.
- Dedicated small pool (2x A100) trial produced median ~38ms under synthetic replay; need real extension traffic test.

Next steps (agreed):
- Finalize POC latency test plan (Arjun to send test harness by 2026-02-14).
- Provide dedicated pricing estimate + egress/quantization cost breakdown (pricing deck link in drive).
- Security: share SOC2 and KMS architecture diagram; schedule security call with their SecOps (target 2026-02-20).
